iterations.theme: Je li dovoljno ići na misu da se spasiš? Propovijed fra Stjepana Brčine o umiranju sebi, životu vječnom i osobnom poznavanju Isusa

sections.subtitle: Otpor koji prati svako dobro djelo
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Stjepan Brčina govori o kušnjama, ogovaranju i ljubomori koje prate Božja djela
sections.content:
Fra Stjepan Brčina propovijed započinje evanđeoskim odlomkom dana u kojem Isusa upozoravaju, a zapravo mu prijete, da će ga ubiti ako ne napusti grad. Propovjednik odmah postavlja ključno pitanje: **povlači li se Isus pred tim prijetnjama?**

Prije odgovora fra Stjepan upozorava na pojavu koju, kako kaže, prepoznaje svatko tko se bavi dobrim djelima, osobito na području evangelizacije. Sve što je Božje, dobro i nadahnuto Duhom često mora proći katarzu. Pritom nabraja ono s čime se takva djela redovito susreću:

- kušnje i napasti,
- izazove i prijetnje,
- ogovaranje,
- ljubomoru.

Propovjednik ističe da se u današnjem Evanđelju doslovno vidi cijeli taj mehanizam okrenut protiv Isusa i njegova djelovanja. Retorički pita je li Isus radio išta loše i odmah odgovara: samo je liječio, naviještao i pomagao drugima, a ipak je mnogima smetao.

U tome fra Stjepan vidi riječ ohrabrenja za vjernike. I oni, kada nešto pokrenu, često dožive sličan pritisak: od njih se traži da prekinu, da odustanu od ideje, da ne guraju projekt. Propovjednik takve prigovore naziva **„mantrama“**, sličnima onima koje su upućivane Isusu.
sections.subtitle_en: The Resistance That Accompanies Every Good Work
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Stjepan Brčina speaks about the trials, gossip, and jealousy that accompany the works of God
sections.content_en:
Fra Stjepan Brčina begins the homily with the Gospel passage of the day in which they warn Jesus, and in fact threaten him, that they will kill him if he does not leave the city. The preacher immediately poses the key question: **does Jesus retreat before these threats?**

Before answering, fra Stjepan warns of a phenomenon that, as he says, everyone who engages in good works recognizes, especially in the field of evangelization. Everything that is of God, good, and inspired by the Spirit often has to undergo catharsis. In doing so, he enumerates what such works regularly encounter:

- trials and temptations,
- challenges and threats,
- gossip,
- jealousy.

The preacher emphasizes that in today's Gospel one can literally see that entire mechanism turned against Jesus and his activity. He rhetorically asks whether Jesus did anything bad and immediately answers: he only healed, proclaimed, and helped others, and yet he bothered many.

In that, fra Stjepan sees a word of encouragement for believers. They too, when they start something, often experience similar pressure: they are asked to stop, to give up on the idea, not to push the project. The preacher calls such objections **“mantras”**, similar to those addressed to Jesus.

sections.subtitle: Isus ne odustaje: „Ja svoje moram završiti“
sections.screenshot_description: Propovjednik prenosi Isusovu odlučnost da nastavi liječiti unatoč prijetnjama
sections.content:
Isusov odgovor, kako ga tumači fra Stjepan Brčina, glasi: **On se ne zaustavlja.** „Ja sam došao da liječim“, poručuje Isus, prvi, drugi i treći dan. Drugim riječima, mora dovršiti ono zbog čega je došao.

Propovjednik naglašava da se Isus ne obazire na to što nekima njegovo djelovanje smeta, pa čak ni na to što ga zbog toga žele ubiti. Zna zašto je tu i zato odgovara da će raditi i danas, dok ne završi svoje poslanje.

U tome fra Stjepan vidi konkretnu pouku: vjernici ne bi trebali odustajati od onoga na što ih Bog potiče i što je dobro, unatoč svakoj riječi, prijetnji i komentaru, iako to nije uvijek ugodno. Kada se nađu u sličnoj situaciji, savjetuje im da se prisjete Isusovih riječi i kažu sami sebi: što god drugi mislili o njima, o njihovu projektu ili dobrom djelu, ne smiju se obeshrabriti **ako je riječ o Božjem djelu**.

Propovjednik to sažima Isusovim riječima: „Ja moram svojim putem danas, sutra, prekosutra“, odnosno moram završiti ono na što me Bog poziva.
sections.subtitle_en: Jesus Does Not Give Up: “I Must Finish My Work”
sections.screenshot_description_en: The preacher conveys Jesus's determination to continue healing despite threats
sections.content_en:
Jesus's response, as interpreted by fra Stjepan Brčina, is: **He does not stop.** “I have come to heal,” Jesus says, the first, the second, and the third day. In other words, he must finish what he came for.

The preacher emphasizes that Jesus pays no mind to the fact that his actions bother some, or even that they want to kill him because of it. He knows why he is here and therefore answers that he will work today as well, until he finishes his mission.

In this, fra Stjepan sees a concrete lesson: believers should not give up on what God urges them to do and what is good, despite every word, threat, and comment, even though it is not always pleasant. When they find themselves in a similar situation, he advises them to recall Jesus's words and say to themselves: whatever others may think about them, about their project or good work, they must not become discouraged **if it is a work of God**.

The preacher summarizes this with Jesus's words: “I must go on my way today, tomorrow, and the next day,” that is, I must finish what God calls me to.

sections.subtitle: Bog poput kvočke koja okuplja svoje piliće
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Stjepan opisuje sliku Boga kao kvočke koja nježno okuplja svoje piliće
sections.content:
Iz istog evanđeoskog odlomka fra Stjepan Brčina izdvaja jednu od najnježnijih slika Boga u Svetom pismu. Bogu se, kako kaže, daje **epitet majke**: On je poput kvočke koja okuplja svoje piliće i nježno se brine za svoj narod i za svakoga pojedinca.

Propovjednik podsjeća da se Božja dobrota vidi kroz cijelu povijest, od početka stvaranja svijeta. Bog kroz povijest toliko puta pokušava sve okupiti, „ali ne ide“. Upravo u toj upornosti očituju se Božja dobrota, nježnost i ljubav prema svakom narodu i svakoj osobi.

Fra Stjepan upozorava na čestu zamku: vjernici takve odlomke slušaju kao povijest, kao nešto što je vrijedilo „u ono vrijeme“. Međutim, ističe on, Bog to misli danas, i to osobno za svakoga. Propovjednik to izražava riječima kojima Bog poručuje vjerniku: **„Ja tebe želim zakriliti, ja tebe želim pod svoje naručje, u svom zagrljaju.“**
sections.subtitle_en: God Like a Hen Gathering Her Brood
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Stjepan describes the image of God as a hen gently gathering her chicks
sections.content_en:
From the same Gospel passage, fra Stjepan Brčina singles out one of the gentlest images of God in Sacred Scripture. God, as he says, is given the **epithet of a mother**: He is like a hen that gathers her chicks and tenderly cares for his people and for every individual.

The preacher reminds us that God's goodness is seen throughout all of history, from the beginning of the creation of the world. Throughout history, God tries so many times to gather everyone, “but it doesn't work.” It is precisely in this persistence that God's goodness, tenderness, and love toward every nation and every person are manifested.

Fra Stjepan warns of a common trap: believers listen to such passages as history, as something that applied “at that time.” However, he emphasizes, God means that today, and personally for everyone. The preacher expresses this with words in which God tells the believer: **“I want to cover you with my wings, I want you under my arms, in my embrace.”**

sections.subtitle: Uoči Svih svetih: o čemu razmišljamo pred grobovima?
sections.screenshot_description: Propovjednik govori o hladnim mramornim pločama i skupim grobnicama
sections.content:
Propovijed je izrečena uoči blagdana Svih svetih i Dušnog dana, kada se obilaze groblja i spominju pokojni. Fra Stjepan Brčina ističe da je to lijepo i kršćanski poticajno jer se vjernici mole za svoje pokojne. Ipak, povezuje to s Isusovom slikom okupljanja: Bog želi čovjekovu dušu i želi da uđe u život vječni.

Zato vjernicima postavlja izravno pitanje: **o čemu razmišljaju dok posjećuju grobove svojih najmilijih?** Svi dolaze i gledaju hladne mramorne ploče u koje su uložene tisuće eura za lijepe mauzoleje, grobnice i citate, „ali nam nitko iz tog groba ne progovara“.

Propovjednik pita muči li ih ikada pitanje gdje su njihovi najmiliji i može li im itko jamčiti da su uopće živi. Spominje i da je i sam ovih dana bio na groblju obići rodbinu. Zanimljivim smatra to što će ovih dana groblja obilaziti i vjernici i nevjernici, koji će jednako paliti i nositi svijeće jer je „to taj dan, sjećamo se“.

Sjećanje na pokojne, naglašava fra Stjepan, sasvim je lijepo. No pitanje ostaje: gdje su oni i gdje su vjernici sami? Kada se među ljudima govori o smrti i životu vječnom, primjećuje on, duhovna dimenzija često se slabo ističe.
sections.subtitle_en: On the Eve of All Saints: What Do We Think About Before Graves?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The preacher speaks about cold marble slabs and expensive tombs
sections.content_en:
The homily was delivered on the eve of the Solemnity of All Saints and All Souls' Day, when cemeteries are visited and the deceased are commemorated. Fra Stjepan Brčina emphasizes that this is beautiful and Christianly encouraging because believers pray for their deceased. Still, he connects this with Jesus's image of gathering: God desires man's soul and wants it to enter eternal life.

Therefore, he asks believers a direct question: **what do they think about while visiting the graves of their loved ones?** Everyone comes and looks at cold marble slabs into which thousands of euros have been invested for beautiful mausoleums, tombs, and quotes, “but no one speaks to us from that grave.”

The preacher asks whether the question of where their loved ones are ever troubles them, and whether anyone can guarantee that they are alive at all. He also mentions that he himself visited the cemetery these days to visit relatives. He considers it interesting that these days both believers and unbelievers will visit cemeteries, lighting and carrying candles just the same because “that is that day, we remember.”

Remembering the deceased, fra Stjepan emphasizes, is entirely beautiful. But the question remains: where are they and where are the believers themselves? When death and eternal life are discussed among people, he observes, the spiritual dimension is often barely emphasized.

sections.subtitle: Obezbijediti grob ili obezbijediti život vječni
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Stjepan uz šalu primjećuje da je grob u Zagrebu skuplji od stana
sections.content:
Fra Stjepan Brčina izdvaja rečenicu koja mu je, kako kaže, „najjača“: **„Ej, jesi sebi obezbijedio grob? Di ćeš ti?“** Ljudi su na zemlji, primjećuje, više zabrinuti kako osigurati grob nego bilo što drugo, jer to danas košta. Tko se želi dostojno pokopati i imati „malo bolju pločicu iznad glave“, mora se za to pripremati od djetinjstva. U Zagrebu je, dodaje uz šalu, grob skoro skuplji od stana.

Zato, nastavlja duhovito, možda nije loše biti podstanar. Podstanar to može prenijeti i na duhovnu razinu: „Kad umrem, ja sam u groblju podstanar.“ Grob, dakle, nije njegov.

Poruka je jasna: grob se može osigurati kakav god, gdje god i s kojom god pločom, ali to ne znači mnogo, jer pokojnik ni tada neće progovoriti kada mu dođu najmiliji. Umjesto rečenice „Moram si obezbijediti grob“, propovjednik poziva vjernike da govore: **„Moram si obezbijediti život vječni.“** Uopće nije bitno kakav je grob i gdje se nalazi.

### Sprovod na kojem su bile dvije osobe

Kao ilustraciju fra Stjepan navodi primjer iz europskih zemalja u kojima su ljudi još otuđeniji pa unaprijed organiziraju cijeli svoj sprovod. Njegova sestra pomagala je jednom usamljenom djedu koji je za života platio organizaciju cijelog sprovoda, **a na sprovodu su bile samo dvije osobe**.

Sve što se tiče zemaljskoga može se unaprijed osigurati, zaključuje propovjednik. No ako se propusti ono bitno, svakodnevna misao „Moram si obezbijediti život vječni“, nitko drugi to neće pripremiti umjesto čovjeka. Slikovito dodaje da nitko neće biti ostavljen da se raspada u sobi ili na ulici: netko će se pobrinuti da tijelo skloni, makar „kao mačku u kartonsku kutiju“. Ali za dušu se nitko drugi ne može pobrinuti osim samog čovjeka, i to **sada, na zemlji**.

### Groblje kao duhovna obnova

Pokojni su, kaže fra Stjepan, svoje učinili. Možda su na sigurnom i osigurali su si život vječni, a vjernici će ih pratiti molitvom. Pitanje je, međutim, gdje su oni sami. Zato poziva da obilazak groblja postane **duhovna obnova**: neka vjernici gledaju spomenike i čitaju godine, pa će vidjeti da umiru i mladi, da umiru svi. A kada netko pronađe vlastito godište, neka se zapita je li si dosad uspio osigurati život vječni.
sections.subtitle_en: Securing a Grave or Securing Eternal Life
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Stjepan jokingly observes that a grave in Zagreb is more expensive than an apartment
sections.content_en:
Fra Stjepan Brčina highlights a sentence that is, as he says, the “strongest” for him: **“Hey, have you secured a grave for yourself? Where will you go?”** People on earth, he observes, are more concerned about securing a grave than anything else, because today that costs money. Whoever wants to be buried decently and have “a slightly better plaque above their head” must prepare for it from childhood. In Zagreb, he adds jokingly, a grave is almost more expensive than an apartment.

Therefore, he continues humorously, perhaps it is not bad to be a tenant. A tenant can transfer that to a spiritual level as well: “When I die, I am a tenant in the cemetery.” The grave, therefore, is not his.

The message is clear: a grave can be secured of whatever kind, wherever, and with whatever plaque, but that does not mean much, because the deceased will not speak even then when loved ones come to him. Instead of the sentence “I must secure a grave for myself,” the preacher invites believers to say: **“I must secure eternal life for myself.”** It does not matter at all what kind of grave it is and where it is located.

### A Funeral Attended by Two People

As an illustration, fra Stjepan cites an example from European countries where people are even more alienated, so they organize their entire funeral in advance. His sister helped a lonely grandfather who during his life paid for the organization of his entire funeral, **and only two people were at the funeral**.

Everything concerning the earthly can be secured in advance, the preacher concludes. But if the essential thing is missed, the everyday thought “I must secure eternal life for myself,” no one else will prepare it instead of the person. Figuratively he adds that no one will be left to decompose in a room or on the street: someone will take care to remove the body, even if “like a cat in a cardboard box.” But for the soul no one else can take care except the person himself, and that **now, on earth**.

### The Cemetery as a Spiritual Renewal

The deceased, says fra Stjepan, have done their part. Perhaps they are safe and have secured eternal life for themselves, and believers will accompany them with prayer. The question, however, is where they themselves are. Therefore, he calls for visiting the cemetery to become a **spiritual renewal**: let believers look at the monuments and read the years, and they will see that young people also die, that everyone dies. And when someone finds their own birth year, let them ask themselves whether they have succeeded in securing eternal life for themselves so far.

sections.subtitle: Pšenično zrno koje ne umre ne propada, nego ostaje samo
sections.screenshot_description: Propovjednik objašnjava da čovjek koji ne umre sebi nije propao, nego je nedovršen
sections.content:
Fra Stjepan Brčina zatim se okreće poznatoj rečenici iz 12. poglavlja Ivanova evanđelja: **„Ako pšenično zrno, pavši na zemlju, ne umre, ostaje samo.“** Pita moralizira li Isus ovdje ili prijeti. Upozorava na detalj koji se lako previdi: Isus ne kaže da će takvo zrno propasti ili istrunuti, nego samo da **ostaje samo**.

To propovjednika vodi na prve stranice Svetoga pisma, gdje nakon stvaranja čovjeka stoji: „Nije dobro da čovjek bude sam.“ Objašnjenje glasi: tko ostane sam, tko ne umre sebi, nije propao, nego je **nedovršen**. Fra Stjepan to namjerno ponavlja: „Nego si nedovršen.“

Bog koji ima epitet majke i okuplja svoju djecu želi dovršiti ono što je u čovjeku započeo. Propovjednik se pritom vraća na Sandijevo ređenje, na kojem biskup kandidatima izgovara riječi: **„Dobri Bog koji je u tebi započeo ovo dobro djelo, neka ga i završi.“**

Bog je čovjeku dao dar, a taj dar je život. Taj se dar, naglašava fra Stjepan, ne dovršava smrću, mramornim pločama ni ukrasima. Vjernici trebaju već sada, za života, umirati sebi kako bi bili dovršeni kada stanu pred Boga.
sections.subtitle_en: A Grain of Wheat That Does Not Die Does Not Perish, but Remains Alone
sections.screenshot_description_en: The preacher explains that a person who does not die to self has not perished, but is unfinished
sections.content_en:
Fra Stjepan Brčina then turns to the well-known sentence from chapter 12 of the Gospel of John: **“Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone.”** He asks whether Jesus is moralizing here or threatening. He warns of a detail that is easily overlooked: Jesus does not say that such a grain will perish or rot, but only that **it remains alone**.

This leads the preacher to the first pages of Sacred Scripture, where after the creation of man it says: “It is not good for man to be alone.” The explanation is: whoever remains alone, whoever does not die to self, has not perished, but is **unfinished**. Fra Stjepan deliberately repeats this: “Rather, you are unfinished.”

God, who has the epithet of mother and gathers his children, wants to finish what he began in man. The preacher in doing so returns to Sandi's ordination, at which the bishop speaks the words to the candidates: **“May the good God who has begun this good work in you bring it to fulfillment.”**

God gave man a gift, and that gift is life. That gift, fra Stjepan emphasizes, is not finished by death, marble slabs, or decorations. Believers need to die to self already now, during life, in order to be finished when they stand before God.

sections.subtitle: Kultura samoostvarenja protiv evanđeoskog umiranja sebi
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Stjepan se obraća mladima o paradoksu umiranja sebi u kulturi samoostvarenja
sections.content:
Posebno se obraćajući mladima, fra Stjepan Brčina upozorava da žive u kulturi koja je izravno suprotna poruci o umiranju sebi. Zato im Božja riječ ponekad zvuči paradoksalno: Bog traži umiranje sebi, a cijeli svijet govori drugačije.

Svijet, kaže propovjednik, neprestano govori o **samoostvarenju**, o tome da treba težiti samo onome što čovjeka ostvaruje. Evanđelje govori suprotno. Fra Stjepan nizom pitanja poziva na razmišljanje:

- Ako se čovjek usredotoči na sebe i ono što misli da će ga ostvariti, hoće li biti sretan?
- Hoće li biti dovršen?
- Je li Bog stvorio čovjeka da misli samo na sebe?
- Ako se okrene samo sebi, nije li ostao sam?

Upravo na to upozorava pšenično zrno: ako ne umre, ostaje samo. Mnogi se danas okreću sebi, primjećuje fra Stjepan, i zato su neostvareni, nedovršeni i nesretni, jer kraj takve sreće nikada ne mogu dosegnuti.

Mudrost koju mnogi ne vide jest u tome da se čovjek najbolje ostvaruje dovršavajući Božji plan koji je u njemu započeo rođenjem, pa i prije toga, „dok sam bio u Božjim mislima“. Bog ne potiče čovjeka da se zatvori i ostane sam, nego **da se otvori drugima**. Čudno je, priznaje propovjednik, da treba umirati i dati svoj život da bi se živjelo, ali Božja riječ pomaže razumjeti tu stvarnost.
sections.subtitle_en: The Culture of Self-Fulfillment Against the Gospel's Dying to Self
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Stjepan addresses the youth about the paradox of dying to self in a culture of self-fulfillment
sections.content_en:
Speaking especially to young people, fra Stjepan Brčina warns that they live in a culture directly opposed to the message of dying to self. That is why God's word sometimes sounds paradoxical to them: God demands dying to self, while the whole world speaks otherwise.

The world, says the preacher, constantly speaks of **self-fulfillment**, about striving only for what fulfills a person. The Gospel says the opposite. Fra Stjepan invites reflection through a series of questions:

- If a person focuses on himself and what he thinks will fulfill him, will he be happy?
- Will he be completed?
- Did God create man to think only of himself?
- If he turns only to himself, has he not remained alone?

It is precisely this that the grain of wheat warns about: if it does not die, it remains alone. Many today turn to themselves, observes fra Stjepan, and are therefore unfulfilled, unfinished, and unhappy, because they can never reach the end of such happiness.

The wisdom that many do not see lies in the fact that man is best fulfilled by completing God's plan that began in him at birth, and even before that, “while I was in God's thoughts.” God does not encourage man to close himself off and remain alone, but **to open himself to others**. It is strange, the preacher admits, that one must die and give one's life in order to live, but the word of God helps to understand that reality.

sections.subtitle: Što znači „mrziti svoj život“?
sections.screenshot_description: Propovjednik tumači hebrejsko stupnjevanje u izrazu „mrziti svoj život“
sections.content:
Fra Stjepan Brčina navodi još jednu rečenicu iz Ivanova evanđelja: **„Tko ljubi svoj život, izgubit će ga, a tko mrzi svoj život na ovome svijetu, sačuvat će ga za život vječni.“** Svjestan je da je mnogi krivo razumiju. Bog ne traži da čovjek mrzi svoj život ili da, poput Joba, proklinje dan kada se rodio.

Propovjednik u rečenici izdvaja tri važna uvida:

1. **Postoje dva života.** Mnogi na groblju misle da je ondje kraj, no rečenica govori o životu na ovom svijetu i o onom drugom.
2. **„Mrziti“ označava stupnjevanje.** U hebrejskom jeziku izraz označava razine, a ne ogorčenje. Smisao je da zemaljski život nije veći od nebeskog. Za Židove je vječni život bio na višem stupnju.
3. **Isus ne najavljuje propast zemaljskog života.** Bog nije stavio čovjeka na svijet da pati, nego da dar života preobrazi u život vječni.

Današnji svijet, kritizira fra Stjepan, živi kao da je zemaljski život najvažniji: borba za ono što se ovdje ima. Na kraju čovjek ne umire sebi i ne osigura život vječni. Ispravan stav jest smatrati život darom od Boga, ali ga staviti na pravo mjesto: **„Mi smo ovdje u prolazu.“** Propovjednik to izražava molitvom: „Hvala ti, Bože, na daru ovog života, ali ja težim za vječnim životom.“

Zato se, kaže, ne smiju gubiti ni dani, ni trenuci, ni minute. Onima koji se pitaju zašto su uopće rođeni odgovara da im je dan dar života kako bi ga preobrazili u život vječni. Ako sada pate, možda ih čeka nebeska nagrada, a to samo Bog zna. Umjesto očaja predlaže molitvu: „Hvala ti, Bože, na daru života. Borit ću se, trudit ću se da ga, uz tvoju milost, preobrazim.“
sections.subtitle_en: What Does It Mean to “Hate One's Life”?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The preacher interprets the Hebrew gradation in the expression “hate one's life”
sections.content_en:
Fra Stjepan Brčina cites another sentence from the Gospel of John: **“Whoever loves his life loses it, and whoever hates his life in this world will preserve it for eternal life.”** He is aware that many misunderstand it. God does not demand that a person hate his life or, like Job, curse the day he was born.

The preacher singles out three important insights in the sentence:

1. **There are two lives.** Many at the cemetery think that is the end, but the sentence speaks of life in this world and of the other.
2. **“To hate” indicates gradation.** In the Hebrew language, the expression indicates levels, not bitterness. The meaning is that earthly life is not greater than heavenly life. For the Jews, eternal life was on a higher degree.
3. **Jesus does not announce the destruction of earthly life.** God did not place man in the world to suffer, but to transform the gift of life into eternal life.

Today's world, fra Stjepan criticizes, lives as if earthly life were the most important: a struggle for what one has here. In the end, man does not die to self and does not secure eternal life. The correct attitude is to consider life a gift from God, but to put it in its proper place: **“We are passing through here.”** The preacher expresses this with a prayer: “Thank you, God, for the gift of this life, but I strive for eternal life.”

Therefore, he says, neither days, nor moments, nor minutes should be wasted. To those who wonder why they were born at all, he answers that they were given the gift of life so they could transform it into eternal life. If they are suffering now, perhaps a heavenly reward awaits them, and only God knows that. Instead of despair, he proposes a prayer: “Thank you, God, for the gift of life. I will fight, I will strive, with your grace, to transform it.”

sections.subtitle: Posjedujemo li mi stvari ili one posjeduju nas?
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Stjepan objašnjava da je čovjek slobodan od onoga što posjeduje samo ako to može dati
sections.content:
Fra Stjepan Brčina ističe da se poruka Evanđelja često čini suprotnom svemu što se događa u svijetu. Nabraja njegove paradokse: **da bi se nešto steklo, mora se dati; da bi se ljubilo, mora se pustiti; da bi se živjelo, mora se umrijeti.**

Poziva vjernike da razmisle o onome što posjeduju, bilo da je riječ o životu, bogatstvu ili talentima, i zapitaju se jesu li od toga slobodni. Mjerilo je jednostavno: ako to mogu davati, slobodni su. Ako ne mogu, onda to posjeduje njih, a ne oni to.

Propovjednik pritom jasno naglašava da nije problem biti bogat, talentiran ili na nekoj poziciji. Važno je koliko je čovjek spreman davati. Ponavlja paradoks: tko želi živjeti, treba umrijeti; tko želi imati, treba davati; tko želi ljubiti, treba poštovati i dati slobodu. Upravo spremnošću da daje i umire za druge čovjek pokazuje da on posjeduje stvari, a ne one njega.

Mnoge, primjećuje, posjeduju materijalne stvari. „Ništa nije problem imati, nego problem je što upravlja s tobom“, kaže fra Stjepan i podsjeća na poznatu rečenicu: **„Tamo gdje ti je blago, tamo ti je i srce.“** Toga se, poručuje, treba čuvati.
sections.subtitle_en: Do We Possess Things or Do They Possess Us?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Stjepan explains that a person is free from what he possesses only if he can give it away
sections.content_en:
Fra Stjepan Brčina emphasizes that the message of the Gospel often seems contrary to everything happening in the world. He enumerates its paradoxes: **in order to gain something, one must give; in order to love, one must let go; in order to live, one must die.**

He invites believers to think about what they possess, whether it is life, wealth, or talents, and ask themselves whether they are free from it. The measure is simple: if they can give it away, they are free. If they cannot, then it possesses them, and not they it.

The preacher at the same time clearly emphasizes that it is not a problem to be rich, talented, or in some position. What matters is how ready a person is to give. He repeats the paradox: whoever wants to live must die; whoever wants to have must give; whoever wants to love must respect and give freedom. It is precisely through readiness to give and die for others that man shows he possesses things, and not they him.

Many, he observes, are possessed by material things. “Having is no problem at all, but the problem is what rules over you,” says fra Stjepan and recalls the well-known sentence: **“Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”** One must beware of that, he says.

sections.subtitle: „Duše su pravednika u ruci Božjoj“ i istina o propovijedima na sprovodima
sections.screenshot_description: Propovjednik govori o očekivanjima da svećenik na sprovodu nahvali pokojnika
sections.content:
Vraćajući se slici kvočke, fra Stjepan Brčina podsjeća da Bog neprestano okuplja ljude i približava ih sebi, kako bi shvatili smisao svog postojanja, ne prokockali vrijeme i ne izgubili život vječni. Kada se sve čini kao teška borba, propovjednik poručuje: nije toliko važno zna li čovjek sve, nego **ima li pouzdanja u Boga** u onome što proživljava i s čime se bori.

Oslanja se pritom na Knjigu Mudrosti: **„Duše su pravednika u ruci Božjoj.“** Vjernici tu, kaže, ništa ne mogu sami. Mogu samo surađivati, zahvaljivati Bogu i opustiti se. Tko je pravedan, umire sebi i otvara se drugima, njemu će Bog dati nagradu. Tko je pak cijeli život sebično živio i mislio samo na sebe, dobit će nagradu onakvu kakav je život živio.

### Sprovodna propovijed nije konačni sud

Fra Stjepan zatim otvoreno govori o sprovodima. Od svećenika se uvijek očekuje lijepa, poticajna i utješna propovijed, po mogućnosti malo uljepšana, uz obvezno hvaljenje pokojnika. To je u redu, kaže, ali **to nije konačni sud**. Pravi ispit savjesti i nagrada dolaze pred Bogom, a ne iz onoga što svećenik kaže na sprovodu.

Spominje i narodnu izreku da o pokojnima treba govoriti samo najbolje, čak i kada se zna da nisu bili dobri. Na to odgovara izravno: **„Poštujmo dok smo živi.“** Ljudi se boje loše govoriti o pokojnima, ali se ne boje loše govoriti o živima. „Ne bojimo se žive pokopati. Tu smo eksperti“, kaže uz oštru opasku da bi neki živima „lopatom u glavu udarali“, dok su na sprovodima „srce drapajuće poruke i govori“. Zaključuje da ljudi nisu tu da sude, jer će dobri Bog svakoga nagraditi.
sections.subtitle_en: “The Souls of the Righteous Are in the Hand of God” and the Truth About Funeral Homilies
sections.screenshot_description_en: The preacher speaks about expectations for a priest to praise the deceased at a funeral
sections.content_en:
Returning to the image of the hen, fra Stjepan Brčina reminds that God constantly gathers people and draws them closer to himself, so that they may understand the meaning of their existence, not gamble away time, and not lose eternal life. When everything seems like a hard struggle, the preacher delivers a message: it is not so important whether a person knows everything, but **whether he has trust in God** in what he is experiencing and struggling with.

In doing so, he relies on the Book of Wisdom: **“The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God.”** Believers, he says, can do nothing here on their own. They can only cooperate, thank God, and relax. Whoever is righteous, dies to self, and opens to others, to him God will give a reward. But whoever lived selfishly their whole life and thought only of themselves will receive a reward according to the kind of life they lived.

### A Funeral Homily Is Not the Final Judgment

Fra Stjepan then speaks openly about funerals. A beautiful, encouraging, and comforting homily is always expected from the priest, preferably slightly embellished, with obligatory praise of the deceased. That is fine, he says, but **that is not the final judgment**. The true examination of conscience and reward come before God, not from what the priest says at a funeral.

He also mentions the popular saying that one should speak only the best about the dead, even when it is known that they were not good. To that he responds directly: **“Let us show respect while we are alive.”** People are afraid to speak ill of the deceased, but they are not afraid to speak ill of the living. “We are not afraid to bury the living. We are experts at that,” he says with a sharp remark that some would hit the living “with a shovel to the head,” while at funerals there are “heart-wrenching messages and speeches.” He concludes that people are not here to judge, because the good God will reward everyone.

sections.subtitle: Isus pitanje okreće: tko će se od vas spasiti?
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Stjepan objašnjava kako Isus pitanje postavljeno u množini okreće prema slušateljima
sections.content:
Koji je cilj svega? Fra Stjepan Brčina odgovara jasno: **biti s Isusom.** Ponovno citira Ivanovo evanđelje, za koje priznaje da ga stalno navodi jer je toliko bogato: „Gdje sam ja, ondje ćete i vi biti.“ Isus pritom ne misli na neki prostor, „muzej ili sobicu“, nego na unutarnje stanje, na bivanje i prebivanje s njim.

Propovjednik zatim podsjeća na evanđeoski odlomak u kojem se Isusa pita koliko će se ljudi spasiti, te na sliku širokog i uskog puta. Slična pitanja, primjećuje, postavljaju i današnji vjernici, koji vole komentirati tuđu vjeru: Tko će se spasiti? Tko je zaslužio? Hoće li se spasiti dobar čovjek koji nije išao na misu? Svećenici, kaže, često dobivaju pitanja poput: „Otac i mater bili su takvi i takvi, hoće li se spasiti?“

Zanimljivo je, ističe fra Stjepan, da Isus na pitanje postavljeno u množini odgovara izravno slušateljima: **tko će se od vas spasiti?** Tako im poručuje da se prestanu baviti spasenjem drugih. Propovjednik poziva okupljene da zamisle da Isus te večeri dođe među njih i postavi im isto pitanje.

Poruka je, kaže, da se vjernici ne bave moraliziranjem članova župne zajednice i vlastitih obitelji, nego vlastitim spasenjem, koje si uz Božju milost i suradnju moraju sami „priuštiti“.

### Opasna sigurnost u vlastito spasenje

Zašto Isus to upozorava farizeje, a i današnje vjernike? Oni koji postavljaju takva pitanja i procjene najčešće su **sigurni u vlastito spasenje**, i zato si dopuštaju moralizirati i procjenjivati. Fra Stjepan pita okupljene je li mudro biti siguran da si spašen. Isus, naglašava, ne traži da se zna nešto o njemu, nego da se poznaje njega.
sections.subtitle_en: Jesus Turns the Question Around: Who Among You Will Be Saved?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Stjepan explains how Jesus turns a question asked in the plural back toward the listeners
sections.content_en:
What is the goal of everything? Fra Stjepan Brčina answers clearly: **to be with Jesus.** He again quotes the Gospel of John, which he admits he constantly cites because it is so rich: “Where I am, there you also will be.” In doing so, Jesus does not mean some space, “a museum or a small room,” but an interior state, being and abiding with him.

The preacher then recalls the Gospel passage in which Jesus is asked how many people will be saved, and the image of the wide and the narrow gate. Similar questions, he observes, are asked by today's believers, who like to comment on the faith of others: Who will be saved? Who deserved it? Will a good person who did not go to Mass be saved? Priests, he says, often receive questions such as: “Father and mother were such and such, will they be saved?”

It is interesting, fra Stjepan emphasizes, that to a question asked in the plural Jesus answers directly to the listeners: **who among you will be saved?** In this way he tells them to stop dealing with the salvation of others. The preacher invites those gathered to imagine Jesus coming among them that evening and asking them the same question.

The message, he says, is that believers should not concern themselves with moralizing about members of the parish community and their own families, but with their own salvation, which with God's grace and cooperation they must “afford” themselves.

### Dangerous Certainty in One's Own Salvation

Why does Jesus warn the Pharisees, and today's believers, about this? Those who ask such questions and make assessments are most often **certain of their own salvation**, and therefore allow themselves to moralize and assess. Fra Stjepan asks those gathered whether it is wise to be certain that you are saved. Jesus, he emphasizes, does not ask that one know something about him, but that one know him.

sections.subtitle: „Jeli smo i pili s tobom“: misa nije automatsko jamstvo spasenja
sections.screenshot_description: Propovjednik upućuje okupljene da pogledaju oltar dok govori o pričesti i spasenju
sections.content:
Središnje pitanje propovijedi, je li dovoljno ići na misu da bi se čovjek spasio, fra Stjepan Brčina otvara odlomkom iz 13. poglavlja Lukina evanđelja. Ljudi Isusu govore: **„Gospodine, mi smo s tobom jeli i pili“**, a on im odgovara: „Ne znam vas odakle ste.“

Propovjednik upućuje okupljene da pogledaju oltar: kršćani danas s Isusom jedu i piju. Je li to jamstvo spasenja? Kritički opisuje katolike koji idu na misu svaki dan i razmišljaju ovako: „Ja se pričešćujem, ja sam spašen, ali sam zabrinut za ostale članove obitelji koji ne idu na misu, svi će završiti u paklu.“ Pita je li to ispravna prosudba.

Odgovor je jasan: **nije dovoljno znati za Isusa, potrebno je poznavati Isusa.** Može se dogoditi da netko jede i pije s Isusom, a da ga ne poznaje. Fra Stjepan opisuje one koji se vole hvaliti da su odrasli uz crkvu, išli na vjeronauk, pjevali u zboru i znaju sve o vjeri. Netko možda zna sve o crkvi i župi, poznaje pola svećenika u Hrvatskoj, pa je čak prijatelj s nekim biskupom. Ključno je, međutim, pitanje: **poznaje li Isusa osobno?**

Da ga osobno poznaje, zaključuje propovjednik, sigurno ne bi procjenjivao tko će se spasiti, a tko neće, niti bi bio siguran u vlastito spasenje.
sections.subtitle_en: “We Ate and Drank with You”: Mass Is Not an Automatic Guarantee of Salvation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The preacher directs those gathered to look at the altar as he speaks about communion and salvation
sections.content_en:
The central question of the homily, whether going to Mass is enough for a person to be saved, fra Stjepan Brčina opens with a passage from chapter 13 of the Gospel of Luke. People say to Jesus: **“Lord, we ate and drank with you”**, and he answers them: “I do not know where you come from.”

The preacher directs those gathered to look at the altar: Christians today eat and drink with Jesus. Is that a guarantee of salvation? He critically describes Catholics who go to Mass every day and think like this: “I receive communion, I am saved, but I am worried about the other family members who do not go to Mass, they will all end up in hell.” He asks whether that is a correct assessment.

The answer is clear: **it is not enough to know of Jesus, it is necessary to know Jesus.** It can happen that someone eats and drinks with Jesus without knowing him. Fra Stjepan describes those who like to boast that they grew up near the church, went to catechism, sang in the choir, and know everything about the faith. Someone may know everything about the church and parish, know half the priests in Croatia, and even be friends with a bishop. The key question, however, is: **do they know Jesus personally?**

If they knew him personally, the preacher concludes, they certainly would not assess who will be saved and who will not, nor would they be certain of their own salvation.

sections.subtitle: Sveci, borba i Izaijino ohrabrenje: „Budite jaki, ne bojte se“
sections.screenshot_description: Fra Stjepan s divljenjem govori o svetom Pavlu i njegovim riječima „Dobar sam boj bio“
sections.content:
Fra Stjepan Brčina podsjeća na riječi Svetoga pisma: **„U grijehu te majka zače.“** Grijeh čovjeka stalno prati, i toga su bili svjesni sveci, koliko god bili sveti. Navodi primjer Don Bosca, koji je, iako je već toliko toga učinio, na kraju života govorio da ima još malo vremena da učini nešto dobro. Vjernici bi, kaže, trebali biti poput svetaca koji su uvijek osjećali težinu grijeha, a ne zavaravati se mišlju da su već spašeni i bezgrešni. Takav stav propovjednik naziva samodopadnošću, hvalisanjem i lažnom uvjerenošću.

Kao drugi primjer uzima svetog Pavla, kojeg s oduševljenjem opisuje: „Koja legenda! Koje obraćenje čovjeka! Koja ljubav prema Isusu! Koja žrtva prema crkvi!“ Pavao je na kraju svoj život sažeo u jednu rečenicu: **„Dobar sam boj bio, trku završio, vjeru sačuvao.“** Fra Stjepan tu rečenicu svodi na jednu riječ: **borba**, i to borba za život vječni, sve do kraja života. Ta borba drži čovjeka budnim kako bi si pripremio život vječni, „a ne grobnicu“.

### Strogi prema sebi, blagi prema drugima

Iz toga proizlazi praktično pravilo: **prema sebi treba biti strog, a prema drugima blag** i usmjeravati ih prema Isusu. Ne obratno, biti strogi suci drugima, „a možda sam ja prvi propao“. Propovjednik poziva vjernike da budu ponizni i iskreni prema sebi, kako bi na kraju poput svetog Pavla mogli reći da su dobar boj bili, trku završili i vjeru sačuvali.

Priznaje da to nije uvijek lako, ali Sveto pismo stalno upozorava, potiče i ohrabruje. Pojašnjava i da u toj borbi čovjek samo surađuje s Bogom i prihvaća dar spasenja. Propovijed završava riječima iz Poslanice Hebrejima, „Upravite ruke svoje klonule i koljena klecava“, te ohrabrenjem proroka Izaije: **„Recite preplašenim srcima: budite jaki, ne bojte se, evo Boga vašega, on sam hita da nas spasi.“** Amen.
sections.subtitle_en: Saints, the Struggle, and Isaiah's Encouragement: “Be Strong, Fear Not”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fra Stjepan speaks with admiration about Saint Paul and his words “I have fought the good fight”
sections.content_en:
Fra Stjepan Brčina recalls the words of Sacred Scripture: **“In sin did my mother conceive me.”** Sin constantly accompanies man, and the saints were aware of this, however holy they were. He cites the example of Don Bosco, who, although he had already done so much, spoke at the end of his life of having a little more time left to do something good. Believers, he says, should be like the saints who always felt the weight of sin, rather than deceiving themselves with the thought that they are already saved and sinless. The preacher calls such an attitude complacency, boasting, and false confidence.

As another example, he takes Saint Paul, whom he describes with enthusiasm: “What a legend! What a conversion of a man! What love for Jesus! What sacrifice for the church!” Paul ultimately summarized his life in one sentence: **“I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.”** Fra Stjepan reduces that sentence to a single word: **struggle**, and specifically the struggle for eternal life, all the way to the end of life. That struggle keeps a person vigilant in order to prepare eternal life for himself, “and not a tomb.”

### Strict with Ourselves, Gentle with Others

From this arises a practical rule: **one should be strict with oneself, and gentle with others** and direct them toward Jesus. Not the other way around, being strict judges of others, “while perhaps I am the first to have perished.” The preacher invites believers to be humble and honest with themselves, so that in the end, like Saint Paul, they can say that they have fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith.

He admits that this is not always easy, but Sacred Scripture constantly warns, encourages, and heartens. He also clarifies that in that struggle man only cooperates with God and accepts the gift of salvation. The homily ends with the words from the Epistle to the Hebrews, “Strengthen your drooping hands and your weak knees,” and with the encouragement of the prophet Isaiah: **“Say to the fearful of heart: be strong, fear not, behold your God, he himself comes to save us.”** Amen.

iterations.theme_en: Is Going to Mass Enough to Be Saved? A Homily by fra Stjepan Brčina on Dying to Self, Eternal Life, and Personally Knowing Jesus
